I continue to pursue innovative solutions that improve our nation’s infrastructure and use of taxpayer dollars. Webster Votes to Pass FY27 NDAA – Advancing President Trumps Peace Through Strength Agenda - Press Releases - United States Congressman Daniel Webster Skip Navigation Press Releases Home News Press Releases Webster Votes to Pass FY27 NDAA – Advancing President Trumps Peace Through Strength Agenda July 22, 2026 Washington, D.C. —  Today,   Florida Congressman Daniel Webster, R-Clermont, voted to pass H.R. 8800, the FY 27 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), legislation that strengthens America’s military, supports our servicemembers, and restores military readiness.   “Today, I voted to pass the FY27 National Defense Authorization Act to ensure America’s military remains the most lethal fighting force in the world,”  said Rep. Webster . “This legislation fulfills Congress’ constitutional responsibility to provide for our common defense by supporting the men and women who serve our country, and investing in the capabilities needed to deter our adversaries and respond to threats.”   The FY27 NDAA strengthens America’s military by rebuilding the defense industrial base, investing in servicemembers and their families, restoring accountability, and providing our Armed Forces with the resources needed to counter adversaries around the world. This legislation advances President Trump’s Peace Through Strength agenda by codifying 22 executive orders and implementing over 40 proposals to ensure America’s military remains equipped and focused on its core missions.   The FY27 NDAA: Provides a 5–7% pay raise and strengthens benefits for servicemembers and military families. Fully funds Department of War support for the Department of Homeland Security's border security mission. Advances President Trump's Peace Through Strength agenda by funding Golden Dome, expanding shipbuilding, strengthening nuclear deterrence, and modernizing our Armed Forces. Authorizes nearly $220 billion for next-generation capabilities, including artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, hypersonics, space-based capabilities, and other emerging technologies. Webster Supports Short-Term Government Funding Bill - Press Releases - United States Congressman Daniel Webster Skip Navigation Press Releases Home News Press Releases Webster Supports Short-Term Government Funding Bill July 21, 2026 Washington, D.C. —  Florida Congressman Daniel Webster, R-Clermont, released the following statement after voting to pass H.R. 9770, the Continuing Appropriations Act, 2027, legislation that fully funds the federal government through December 4, 2026.   “Today, I voted to pass legislation to keep the government funded at current levels and provide certainty for the American people. While I generally oppose funding the government through continuing resolutions, allowing Democrats to shut down the government would only create instability for hardworking Americans. House Republicans have acted early by advancing all twelve appropriations bills from committee and it is shameful that Democrats in the Senate have forced delays solely for political purposes.”   ### Permalink: https://webster.house.gov/2026/7/webster-supports-short-term-government-funding-bill Press Releases Video Statements

Webster Votes to Pass America First National Security Funding Bill - Press Releases - United States Congressman Daniel Webster Skip Navigation Press Releases Home News Press Releases Webster Votes to Pass America First National Security Funding Bill July 15, 2026 Washington, D.C. —  Florida Congressman Daniel Webster, R-Clermont, released the following statement after voting to pass H.R. 8595, the Fiscal year 2027 National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act.    “This legislation rejects the Washington presumption that nothing can be cut from the budget in order to fund our nation’s priorities without increasing the deficit,”  said Rep. Webster . “Through regular order, we are advancing America First policies that strengthen our national security, support key allies, confront our adversaries, and eliminate wasteful spending on programs that do not serve America’s interests. While there is more work to be done to restore fiscal discipline, this bill is an important step toward ensuring our national security and foreign policy priorities are accountable to the American people.”    The FY27 National Security and Department of State Appropriations Act restores fiscal responsibility by reducing spending by six percent while ensuring the United States continues to invest in our core national security priorities. The bill advances America’s national security and economic interests, reinforces oversight of foreign aid programs, eliminates spending on wasteful programs, and ensures taxpayer dollars are used to benefit American security.   Key provisions include: Reduces spending by 6% below the previously enacted level.  Ensures foreign assistance advances America’s national interests  Supports key allies like Israel and Taiwan. Funds efforts to counter Chinese influence in the Indo-Pacific. Strengthens President Trump’s efforts to combat fentanyl trafficking and transnational crime.
